## Overview

Reach a GaiaDesk desk from a script, an agent or a terminal.

```text
gaiadesk-cli <command> [options]
```

`gaiadesk-cli <command> --help` (or `gaiadesk-cli help <command>`) for each one.
`gaiadesk-cli --version [--json]` — the release (and, with --json, a feature list to detect).

```text
JSON (every command that takes --json): failures are one envelope on stdout,
  {"error":{"kind":"usage|refused|unreachable|connection_lost|failed|protocol","message":"…"}},
  with the same exit codes as without it. `gaiadesk-cli help json` for the shapes and what changed.
```

```text
credentials (every command that reaches a desk — the same rule for all of them):
  --code <c> --allow-code-in-argv   the code on the command line (refused without the second flag:
                                    every user on this machine can read a command line)
  --token-file <file>               a scoped agent token (`gaiadesk-cli token create`), chmod 600
  $GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE              the same, from the environment
  $GAIADESK_CODE                    the desk's code or password
  otherwise an echo-free prompt — only on a terminal; without one the command fails and says so.
The connection is held for later commands (--persist, default 10m), per desk AND credential.
Docs: https://gaiadesk.net/docs/cli-for-agents
```

## devices

The desks you can reach.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli devices [--json] [--probe] [-d <desk-id>] [--token-file <file>]
```

With no credential flags it uses this machine's sign-in — usually the GaiaDesk app's account —
and says so on stderr ("signed in as &lt;email&gt; (from the GaiaDesk app on this machine)"); --json
adds "identity": {"source": "app|login|token|none", "account": "&lt;email&gt;"|null} (see `whoami`).

Lists, merged by desk id: your account's and your team's desks (from the GaiaDesk server, when
this machine is signed in), desks paired with this machine (LAN), GaiaDesk Mesh peers, and desks
this CLI has connected to before — with hostname, OS, version, owner and last seen.

```text
ONLINE is presence only: the desk's GaiaDesk holds a connection to the server (or the LAN/Mesh
saw it). `online(silent 5m)`: the server has not heard from it for that long — likely a dead
connection. REACH is whether commands actually get through: this machine's last connect to it
(`ok 4 min ago via Mesh`) or last failure and where it stuck (`failed 2 min ago: relay_down`):
  no_route            not found on the LAN or Mesh        relay_down       the server did not answer
  desk_not_answering  asked, never answered: busy, stuck, or waiting for someone to approve
  asleep / restarting the desk is asleep / updating        no_data_channel  accepted, no path carried it
  agent_not_answering connected, but its GaiaDesk did not answer a round trip (probe)
```

**Options**

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--probe` | dial each desk NOW (4 at a time, 15s each): route and round-trip time, or the step it failed at; exits 1 if a dialled desk was unreachable. Presents a token only to the desk it names, and a code ($GAIADESK_CODE, --code) only with -d; a desk with no credential is not dialled |
| `-d, --desk-id <id>` | only this desk |
| `--json` | one JSON object: devices[] with online, reachable, last_ok, last_failure, probe, signal_idle_secs, anytime |

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## whoami

Who this CLI is signed in as.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli whoami [--json]
```

```text
The GaiaDesk account the CLI presents to the server (to list your desks, to reach them through
it), and where that sign-in comes from:
  app     the GaiaDesk app on this machine is signed in, and the CLI uses its account
  login   `gaiadesk-cli login`
  token   $GAIADESK_TOKEN (or an SDK's account_token)
  none    nobody: only desks on the LAN, on Mesh, or reached with a code or token
--json: {"source":"app|login|token|none","account":"<email>"|null}. Exit 0 signed in, 1 not.
```

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## exec

Run ONE command on a desk and exit with its exit code.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli exec --desk-id <id> [options] -- <command> [args...]
```

Like `ssh host cmd`: the command's stdout goes to stdout and its stderr to stderr, unaltered (no
echo, no prompt, no escape codes, no console width — plain pipes, on Windows too); stdin is closed
unless -i; the exit code is the command's own. With an agent token, the token needs the `exec`
scope; without it the desk refuses the command (exit 254, with the desk's reason).

```text
WHICH SHELL — the default is the desk's own shell, and it differs by desk:
  macOS/Linux  `$SHELL -l -c '<line>'` — the desk user's LOGIN shell (zsh on a Mac): their PATH and
               profile, and zsh syntax. For portable POSIX scripts, say so: --shell sh (/bin/sh -c).
  Windows      cmd.exe (/d /v:off /s /c), switched to UTF-8 (chcp 65001) first. --shell pwsh for
               PowerShell (pwsh, else Windows PowerShell), with UTF-8 output.
  `--json` and `--verbose` print the shell the desk actually used.
```

**Options**

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--desk-id <id>` | the desk (-d) |
| `--shell <s>` | default \| sh \| bash \| zsh \| pwsh (or powershell) \| cmd \| none (see above; pwsh starts with -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive and a decoded -Command: no prompt, no CLIXML progress on stderr) ONE argument after `--` is a command line for that shell, verbatim (`-- 'ls \| wc -l'`); SEVERAL are separate arguments, each quoted for that shell so the program receives exactly them. `none` runs the program directly with that argument vector. |
| `-n, --no-stdin` | stdin is closed (the default) |
| `-i, --stdin` | forward this terminal's stdin to the command |
| `--timeout <dur>` | stop the command after &lt;dur&gt; (30s, 10m, 2h; 0 = never; default 30m) |
| `--connect-timeout <dur>` | give up reaching the desk after &lt;dur&gt; (default 60s); the error names the step that did not finish (route, server, LAN, the desk's answer) |
| `--cwd <dir>` | start the command in &lt;dir&gt; on the desk (relative: from the desk user's home). A token confined to a directory may only name one inside it — anything else is refused (254); a directory that is not there fails (1) |
| `-e, --env KEY=VALUE` | set an environment variable for the command (repeatable; a later one wins). Values go to the desk in the request and are never logged. |
| `-e, --env KEY` | the same, with the value of $KEY here — keeps a secret off this command line (which other users of this machine can read) |
| `--env-file <file>` | KEY=VALUE lines (# comments, blank lines and `export ` allowed) |
| `--json` | print one JSON object: {exit, remote_code, stdout, stderr, duration_ms, desk, route, mode, shell, timed_out, error, notes, truncated}. `error` is null, or {kind, message[, reason]} (`gaiadesk-cli help json`). A program Windows Smart App Control / WDAC refused to start has reason "blocked_by_os_policy" (and the message says where it is logged) |
| `--json-stream` | one JSON object per line AS IT RUNS: {"event":"stdout","data":…}, {"event":"stderr","data":…}, then {"event":"exit",…} (--json's object without the output) or {"event":"error","exit":N,"error":{…}} |
| `-v, --verbose` | say on stderr how it ran: route, mode (pipes), shell, exit, time |
| `--persist <dur>` | keep the connection open for later commands for &lt;dur&gt; idle (default 10m, or $GAIADESK_PERSIST; 0 = connect fresh every time) |
| `-q, --quiet` | no progress lines on stderr |

**Examples**

```sh
gaiadesk-cli exec -d 123456789 --shell sh -- 'uname -a; df -h /'
gaiadesk-cli exec -d 123456789 -- hostname   # a Windows desk: cmd.exe
gaiadesk-cli exec -d 123456789 --shell pwsh -- 'Get-Service | Where-Object Status -eq Running'
gaiadesk-cli exec -d 123456789 --cwd /srv/app --json-stream -- 'make test'
```

```text
credentials (see `gaiadesk-cli --help` for the order):
  --token-file <file>      a scoped agent token (or $GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE)
  --code <code>            the desk's code — refused unless --allow-code-in-argv too (prefer
                           $GAIADESK_CODE or the prompt: argv is visible to other users)
```

```text
exit codes:
  0-255  the command's own exit code
  124    --timeout ran out (the command was stopped)
  130    interrupted (Ctrl-C)
  254    the desk refused (wrong code, a token without the scope, no permission, declined)
  255    gaiadesk-cli's own error (offline, unreachable, bad arguments)
```

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## shell

A terminal on a desk, like `ssh host`.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli shell --desk-id <id> [options]                  (interactive)
gaiadesk-cli shell --desk-id <id> [options] -- <command>     (one command, like exec)
<script> | gaiadesk-cli shell --desk-id <id> [options]       (a script on stdin)
```

On a terminal, an interactive shell (the desk's own: your login shell on macOS/Linux, cmd.exe on
Windows) at your terminal's size. Not on a terminal — a command after `--`, or a script piped in
— it runs over plain pipes like `exec`: stdout and stderr apart, no prompt, no echo, no console
width, and the exit code is the remote command's (a script's: its last command's). --shell sh
runs a script with /bin/sh instead of the desk user's login shell (zsh on a Mac).

**Options**

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--desk-id <id>` | the desk (-d) |
| `--shell <s>` | non-interactive: default \| sh \| pwsh \| cmd (see `exec --help`) |
| `--timeout <dur>` | non-interactive: stop it after &lt;dur&gt; (default 30m; 0 = never) |
| `--json` | non-interactive: one JSON object, as `exec --json` |
| `--cwd <dir>` | start the shell (or the command, or the script) in &lt;dir&gt; on the desk, as `exec --cwd`: inside a confined token's directory or refused (254) |
| `--persist <dur>` | share a held connection (see `exec --help`; default 10m) |
| `--connect-timeout <dur>` | give up reaching the desk after &lt;dur&gt; (default 60s) |
| `-v, --verbose` | say on stderr how it ran (non-interactive) |
| `-q, --quiet` | no progress lines |

```text
exit codes (never 0 unless the remote shell or command said 0; the reason is always on stderr):
  0-255  the remote shell's / command's own exit code
  124    --timeout ran out          130  interrupted (Ctrl-C)
  253    remote error: the connection was lost mid-session, or the desk ended the terminal
  254    refused: wrong code, a token without the `exec` scope, no control, declined
  255    could not connect: offline, unreachable, timed out (bad arguments too)
An agent token needs the `exec` scope.
```

```text
credentials (see `gaiadesk-cli --help` for the order):
  --token-file <file>      a scoped agent token (or $GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE)
  --code <code>            the desk's code — refused unless --allow-code-in-argv too (prefer
                           $GAIADESK_CODE or the prompt: argv is visible to other users)
```

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## cp

Copy files or folders to or from a desk, like `scp`.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli cp [-r] [--json] [-v] <local> <desk-id>:<path>      (upload)
gaiadesk-cli cp [-r] [--json] [-v] <desk-id>:<path> <local>      (download)
```

Resumable: run the same copy again and an interrupted file continues where it stopped (each file
is checked by SHA-256). A remote path is relative to the desk user's home; a trailing / means
"into that folder". A token needs the `cp` scope.

**Options**

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-r, --recursive` | copy a folder |
| `--json` | one JSON summary of what moved — and nothing else: no progress or summary line on stderr (add -v for them) |
| `-v, --verbose` | with --json, the progress lines on stderr too |

Windows paths are shown without the \\?\ prefix.

```text
credentials (see `gaiadesk-cli --help` for the order):
  --token-file <file>      a scoped agent token (or $GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE)
  --code <code>            the desk's code — refused unless --allow-code-in-argv too (prefer
                           $GAIADESK_CODE or the prompt: argv is visible to other users)
```

exit codes: 0 done; 1 it ran and did not succeed (a file failed, no such job);
254 the desk refused (credential, a token without the scope, permission); 255 this CLI's own error.
The session is the held one `exec` and `shell` use (per desk and credential; $GAIADESK_PERSIST).

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## forward

Forward a local port to a desk, like `ssh -L`.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli forward [--json] <desk-id>:[<host>:]<port> localhost:<port> [more pairs…]
```

Listens on localhost:&lt;port&gt; here and carries each connection to &lt;port&gt; on the desk (or to &lt;host&gt;,
as the desk reaches it). Runs until Ctrl-C. Reverse forwarding (-R) is not supported. Needs
control of the desk; a token needs the `forward` scope.

**Options**

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | print {"event":"listening",…} once each port is open |

```text
credentials (see `gaiadesk-cli --help` for the order):
  --token-file <file>      a scoped agent token (or $GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE)
  --code <code>            the desk's code — refused unless --allow-code-in-argv too (prefer
                           $GAIADESK_CODE or the prompt: argv is visible to other users)
```

exit codes: 0 done; 1 it ran and did not succeed (a file failed, no such job);
254 the desk refused (credential, a token without the scope, permission); 255 this CLI's own error.
The session is the held one `exec` and `shell` use (per desk and credential; $GAIADESK_PERSIST).

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## run

Start a named background job on a desk.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli run --detach --name <job> --desk-id <id> [options] -- <command…>
```

ONE argument after `--` is the command line itself, given to the desk's shell verbatim (cmd.exe on
Windows, sh on macOS/Linux): `-- 'msbuild app.sln /m'`, `-- 'make -j8 && make install'`. Several
arguments are separate words, each quoted for THAT desk's shell; on Windows an argument holding a
cmd metacharacter (&amp; | &lt; &gt; ^ % ! ( ) ") is refused — give the whole line as one argument instead.

THE way to run long work on a desk (builds, tests, renders, backups): the job belongs to the desk's
GaiaDesk host, not to this connection — it keeps running when this command, the connection, or
the terminal you ran it from ends, and when GaiaDesk itself restarts. Read it with `logs` (-f to
follow), list it with `ps`, stop it (and everything it started) with `kill`. On Windows it runs in
a Job object of its own, out of the session's; on macOS/Linux in a session of its own (setsid).
Do not background work inside `exec` (`start /b`, `nohup … &`): exec ends its whole process tree.
For a command whose output you wait for, use `exec`. Needs control of the desk; a token needs the
`jobs` scope.

**Options**

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--cwd <dir>` | the directory the job starts in on the desk (inside a confined token's directory, or refused) |
| `--shell <s>` | sh \| bash \| zsh \| cmd \| pwsh (or powershell): the shell that runs the command (default: sh -c on macOS/Linux, cmd /c on Windows) |
| `-e, --env KEY[=VALUE]` | an environment variable for the job (repeatable; a bare KEY takes $KEY here); never logged |
| `--env-file <file>` | KEY=VALUE lines, as `exec --env-file` |
| `--priority low\|normal\|high` | CPU priority (alias --nice). Windows: the job's priority class; macOS/Linux: nice 10 for low (+ background QoS on a Mac), -5 for high (high needs a GaiaDesk host running as root) |
| `--cpu <percent>` | at most this share of the WHOLE machine, 1-100 (Windows: Job object hard cap; Linux: cgroup v2 CPUQuota; macOS, or Linux without cgroups: GaiaDesk pauses the job to hold it there) |
| `--mem <MB>` | at most this much memory for the job and everything it starts (512, 2G). Windows: Job object limit (allocations past it fail); Linux: cgroup v2 MemoryMax, else RLIMIT_AS + GaiaDesk's watchdog; macOS: GaiaDesk stops the job past it — `ps` shows `killed (memory limit …)` |
| `--keep-awake` | the desk does not idle-sleep while the job runs (released when it ends); --no-keep-awake overrides a desk whose default is on |
| `--json` | the job as JSON (with `limits` and how the desk enforces them); a failure is the envelope (`gaiadesk-cli help json`) |

A job a program in it was refused by Windows Smart App Control / WDAC ends as
`exited (blocked by Windows Smart App Control / WDAC)` with reason "blocked_by_os_policy".
Wait for one to end with `gaiadesk-cli wait <job>`.

**Examples**

```sh
gaiadesk-cli run -d --name build --desk-id 234567890 --priority low --cpu 50 -- 'msbuild app.sln /m'
gaiadesk-cli run -d --name nightly --desk-id 123456789 --keep-awake --mem 4G -- ./nightly.sh
```

```text
credentials (see `gaiadesk-cli --help` for the order):
  --token-file <file>      a scoped agent token (or $GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE)
  --code <code>            the desk's code — refused unless --allow-code-in-argv too (prefer
                           $GAIADESK_CODE or the prompt: argv is visible to other users)
```

exit codes: 0 done; 1 it ran and did not succeed (a file failed, no such job);
254 the desk refused (credential, a token without the scope, permission); 255 this CLI's own error.
The session is the held one `exec` and `shell` use (per desk and credential; $GAIADESK_PERSIST).

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## ps

List a desk's background jobs.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli ps --desk-id <id> [--json]
```

Each job's name, state (running, exited, killed, lost — and why a desk stopped it, e.g.
`killed (memory limit 512 MB)`), exit code, pid, log size, its caps (priority, cpu, mem,
keep-awake) and command. `--json` prints {"jobs":[…]} and adds `limits` and `enforcement`: how this desk enforces each cap, and what it could
not. A token needs the `jobs` scope.

```text
credentials (see `gaiadesk-cli --help` for the order):
  --token-file <file>      a scoped agent token (or $GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE)
  --code <code>            the desk's code — refused unless --allow-code-in-argv too (prefer
                           $GAIADESK_CODE or the prompt: argv is visible to other users)
```

exit codes: 0 done; 1 it ran and did not succeed (a file failed, no such job);
254 the desk refused (credential, a token without the scope, permission); 255 this CLI's own error.
The session is the held one `exec` and `shell` use (per desk and credential; $GAIADESK_PERSIST).

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## wait

Block until a background job ends.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli wait <job> --desk-id <id> [--timeout <dur>] [--json]
```

Returns when the job is no longer running, and exits with ITS exit code (a job that was killed
or lost, with no code: 1). The desk holds the request until then (an older desk is asked every
second instead). A token needs the `jobs` scope.

**Options**

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--timeout <dur>` | give up after &lt;dur&gt; (30s, 10m, 2h): exit 124, the job still running |
| `--json` | the job as JSON, as it ended (or as it stands at the timeout) |

exit codes: the job's own exit code; 1 no such job, or it ended without one; 124 --timeout ran
out; 254 the desk refused; 255 this CLI's own error (offline, unreachable, bad arguments).

```text
credentials (see `gaiadesk-cli --help` for the order):
  --token-file <file>      a scoped agent token (or $GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE)
  --code <code>            the desk's code — refused unless --allow-code-in-argv too (prefer
                           $GAIADESK_CODE or the prompt: argv is visible to other users)
```

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## kill

Stop a background job and everything it started.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli kill <job> --desk-id <id> [--json]
```

```text
credentials (see `gaiadesk-cli --help` for the order):
  --token-file <file>      a scoped agent token (or $GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE)
  --code <code>            the desk's code — refused unless --allow-code-in-argv too (prefer
                           $GAIADESK_CODE or the prompt: argv is visible to other users)
```

exit codes: 0 done; 1 it ran and did not succeed (a file failed, no such job);
254 the desk refused (credential, a token without the scope, permission); 255 this CLI's own error.
The session is the held one `exec` and `shell` use (per desk and credential; $GAIADESK_PERSIST).

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## stats

What a desk is doing right now.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli stats --desk-id <id> [--json]      (or: gaiadesk-cli stats <id>)
```

CPU busy % (a short sample), load average (not on Windows), free and total memory, free space on
each volume, uptime, and how many background jobs are running — from the desk's own GaiaDesk.

**Options**

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-d, --desk-id <id>` | the desk |
| `--json` | one JSON object: hostname, os, os_version, cpu_percent, cpus, load, mem_total_mb, mem_free_mb, disks[{mount,total_mb,free_mb}], uptime_secs, jobs_running |

```text
credentials (see `gaiadesk-cli --help` for the order):
  --token-file <file>      a scoped agent token (or $GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE)
  --code <code>            the desk's code — refused unless --allow-code-in-argv too (prefer
                           $GAIADESK_CODE or the prompt: argv is visible to other users)
```

exit codes: 0 done; 1 it ran and did not succeed (a file failed, no such job);
254 the desk refused (credential, a token without the scope, permission); 255 this CLI's own error.
The session is the held one `exec` and `shell` use (per desk and credential; $GAIADESK_PERSIST).

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## token

Scoped, expiring agent tokens, administered by the desk's owner.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli token create --desk <id>[,<id>…] [--name <n>] [--expires 7d] [--scope exec,cp,jobs]
                          [--cwd <dir on the desk>] [--low-priv] [--out <file>] [--json]
gaiadesk-cli token list --desk <id> [--json]         ({"tokens":[…]})
gaiadesk-cli token revoke --desk <id> (<name|id> | --all-for-desk) [--account]
```

**Subcommands:** `create`, `list`, `revoke`

The credential to give an AI agent instead of the desk's password. Owner only: these present the
desk's unattended password (never a token). Defaults: 7 days, scopes exec,cp,jobs.
Scopes: exec (one command), shell (an interactive shell), cp, forward, jobs (= run), screen.
--cwd: the token's commands, shells and jobs start there and every path it copies must be inside
it (links resolved). --low-priv: they run as the desk's low-privilege agent user (Settings →
Agent access on the desk), or are refused. The desk enforces both. Several desks: one token each,
all in one --out file. `--out` writes a private (0600) file for --token-file; otherwise each token
is printed once. A revoke takes effect at once: its sessions are dropped and its jobs stopped;
--account revokes through the GaiaDesk server as the account signed in here (no password).

exit codes: 0 done; 1 it ran and did not succeed (a file failed, no such job);
254 the desk refused (credential, a token without the scope, permission); 255 this CLI's own error.
The session is the held one `exec` and `shell` use (per desk and credential; $GAIADESK_PERSIST).

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## audit

What agent tokens did on a desk.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli audit --desk <id> [--token <name|id>] [--limit 50] [--account] [--json]
```

--json prints {"events":[…]}.

Newest first: each command an agent token ran (with its directory, exit code and how long it took),
each shell line, each copy (paths and bytes), forward, job and refusal — kept 90 days on the desk.
Reads the desk's own log with its unattended password; --account reads the GaiaDesk server's copy
as the account signed in here instead.

exit codes: 0 done; 1 it ran and did not succeed (a file failed, no such job);
254 the desk refused (credential, a token without the scope, permission); 255 this CLI's own error.
The session is the held one `exec` and `shell` use (per desk and credential; $GAIADESK_PERSIST).

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

status: every peer (desk id, Mesh address, online, OS). ip: one desk's stable Mesh address, for

## measure

The round trip and clock offset to a desk.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli measure <desk-id> [--count <n>] [--json]
```

Pings the desk over the session's data plane (default 20, 100 ms apart) and prints the round
trip (p50/p95/max, the desk's own handling time taken out) and the offset between the two
clocks with its uncertainty. Screen-to-screen and input-to-screen latency need a viewer: in a
session, Actions → Measure latency (or GAIADESK_MEASURE_LATENCY=1 for the desktop app).

**Options**

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-c, --count <n>` | how many pings (1–1000) |
| `--json` | one JSON object |

```text
credentials (see `gaiadesk-cli --help` for the order):
  --token-file <file>      a scoped agent token (or $GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE)
  --code <code>            the desk's code — refused unless --allow-code-in-argv too (prefer
                           $GAIADESK_CODE or the prompt: argv is visible to other users)
```

exit codes: 0 done; 1 it ran and did not succeed (a file failed, no such job);
254 the desk refused (credential, a token without the scope, permission); 255 this CLI's own error.
The session is the held one `exec` and `shell` use (per desk and credential; $GAIADESK_PERSIST).

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## disconnect

Close a held connection.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli disconnect (--desk-id <id> | --all) [--json]      ({"closed":["<desk-id>",…]})
```

exec and shell keep a desk's connection open for --persist (default 10m) so later commands skip the
handshake. This closes it now.

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## agent-connect

Check an agent token against a desk.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli agent-connect --desk-id <id> [--server <wss://host/ws>] [--token <t>] [--json]
```

Opens an agent session, takes one screenshot, and exits. The token comes from --token or
$GAIADESK_AGENT_TOKEN and is never printed. --json: {"desk_id","ok":true,"screenshot":{"width","height"}},
or the error envelope.

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## agent run

Drive a desk with a model (Agent Access).

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli agent run --desk-id <id> (--task <text> | --task-file <path>) [options]
```

```text
options: --model <m> --max-steps <n> --max-duration <secs> --long-edge <px> --token-budget <n>
         --max-tokens <n> --allow-domain <d> --server <wss://…/ws> --token <t> --name <n>
         --out-dir <dir> --report <path> --junit <path>
The model key comes from $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; the agent token from --token or $GAIADESK_AGENT_TOKEN.
Exit: 0 passed, 1 failed, 2 no verdict, 3 stopped by a human, 4 refused; 254/255 as elsewhere.
```

## mcp

GaiaDesk tools over the Model Context Protocol.

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli mcp [--http [--bind <ip>] [--port <n>] [--allow-origin <o>]] [--server <wss://…/ws>]
                 [--allow-domain <d>] [--audit-dir <dir>]
```

stdio by default. Screen tools need an agent token in $GAIADESK_AGENT_TOKEN. The desk tools —
gaiadesk_exec (one command, exit code and separate streams; `env`, `shell`), gaiadesk_copy_files,
gaiadesk_job_run (`env`, `shell`), gaiadesk_job_list, gaiadesk_job_logs, gaiadesk_job_wait,
gaiadesk_job_kill, gaiadesk_forward_\* — ride the held connections the CLI uses and present, over stdio, an agent token
from $GAIADESK_TOKEN_FILE, else $GAIADESK_CODE, else the agent token; over HTTP, only the agent token.
The desk tools return `structuredContent` and list an `outputSchema`.

Protocol: the standard lifecycle (initialize → notifications/initialized → requests, ping) at
2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05 — over HTTP with an Mcp-Session-Id — and the
stateless 2026-07-28 revision (per-request _meta, server/discover, mirrored headers).

Tool names are [a-zA-Z0-9_-] (gaiadesk_exec, gaiadesk_screenshot, …).

```text
--audit-dir <dir>  where each session's record goes (default: mcp-audit in this user's GaiaDesk
                   data directory — never the directory the client started the server in).
```

## schema

The JSON Schema of every --json shape.

```text

```

One JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) with every result, error, request and event type of
gaiadesk-client — and so of every `--json` output — under $defs (`x-roots` names the ones a call
returns or takes). scripts/gen-sdk-types.mts turns it into TypeScript and Python types.

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## login, logout

Sign this CLI in (shows a code to approve in a browser)

**Usage**

```text
gaiadesk-cli login [--json]    sign this CLI in (shows a code to approve in a browser)
gaiadesk-cli logout [--json]   sign this CLI out (ends its Atlas session and sign-in)
```

The server is $GAIADESK_SERVER (a wss:// URL), else production.

```text
--json: one JSON object per line on stdout. login: first
  {"event":"code","verification_uri":…,"verification_uri_complete":…,"user_code":…}
(show it to the person who approves), then {"event":"signed_in","email":…} — or the error
envelope {"error":{"kind","message"}}. logout: {"event":"signed_out"}.
```

> **JSON:** with `--json` this command prints one JSON document on stdout (or the error envelope `{"error":{"kind","message"}}` on failure). The exact shape is defined in the JSON Schema printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; see also [JSON output](#json-output).

## JSON output

The shapes a program can rely on.

```text
ERRORS: every command that takes --json prints, on stdout, when it fails:
  {"error": {"kind": "<kind>", "message": "<a sentence>", "reason": "<finer cause, sometimes>"}}
kind is one of six:
  usage            bad arguments — fix the call                          (exit 255)
  refused          the desk or server said no: credential, scope, permission, a confined
                   token's directory                                       (exit 254)
  unreachable      the desk or server could not be reached: offline, unknown id, no route,
                   timed out (`reason`: offline, unknown_desk, not_online, network,
                   not_signed_in, timeout)                                (exit 255)
  connection_lost  reached, and the connection went away mid-request      (exit 255; shell 253)
  failed           allowed, and it did not succeed: no such job, a file failed, a local error
                                                                         (exit 1, or 255)
  protocol         the desk answered something this CLI cannot use — usually a GaiaDesk too
                   old for the request (update it)                         (exit 255)
Refused-vs-failed comes from the desk itself (a field on its answer), not from its words.
exec/shell --json keep their whole object and put the same {kind, message, reason} in `error`.
The human sentence still goes to stderr.

SHAPES: ps {"jobs":[…]} · token list {"tokens":[…]} · audit {"events":[…]} · devices {"devices":[…]}
  · logs {"job","output"} (-f: events) · mesh ip {"desk_id","mesh_ip","renamed_to"}
  · wait: the job {"name","state","exit_code",…} · whoami {"source","account"}
  · devices also {"identity":{"source","account"}} · disconnect {"closed":[…]} · agent-connect {"desk_id","ok","screenshot"}
  · login/logout: events {"event":"code"|"signed_in"|"signed_out"}
  · exec --json-stream: {"event":"stdout"|"stderr","data"} … {"event":"exit"|"error"}
  · --version --json {"name","version","features":[…],"mcp_protocol_versions"}
```

The JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) of every result, error, request and event type is printed by `gaiadesk-cli schema --json`; the SDKs generate their types from it.
